change_reason: Protocol v4 (accepted decision 0132, issues #349 and #351, part of #163) adds what a user of a mail mock pays to operate it. It keeps protocol v3's nine targets, products, corpus, statistics and capabilities, and replaces the unenforced local budget with an enforced one: every target runs in a driver-owned cgroup v2 leaf limited to 2 CPUs, 2048 MiB, no swap and 4096 tasks, pinned to two cores by affinity, sampled every 100 ms and removed with cgroup.kill. Story A of 0132 builds the cost section (four profiles at 1, 8 and 32 sessions); the API, wait and test-execution sections are owed by later stories and listed under unresolved, so this draft cannot freeze. Every capped target is launched with the same 150,000 cap. It is a separate run with a separate denominator: no table or statistic merges a v4 cell with a v2 or v3 cell, and v3 stays as frozen.

claim.statement: Measures the digest-checked executables named in products, launched with the lock's fixed launch. For an official target each release tag's commit is attributed source context only: nothing ties an executable to it, so no built-from, equivalence or same-build claim is made. Mailpit, MailHog, MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket are official artifacts, and MailSlurper's official release executable does not start with its default SQLite storage (a CGO_ENABLED=0 build; a published result, so that row is blocked and carries no number); the mailslurper-source-build row is a different executable, MailSlurper release-1.15.0 built from source with cgo on a host glibc (unpinned runtime), not an official artifact, and both MailSlurper executables report v1.14.1 under tag release-1.15.0; GreenMail is an official jar bound to its Maven Central artifact by the registry's own checksum (integrity against that checksum; authenticity not verified), run on a pinned JRE; the alkemio-mailslurper row is a third-party patched image's extracted binary, run natively on the musl loader pinned from the image's own layer and never counted as an official competitor row, and the swarmail candidate is neither. MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket tag their releases lightweight, which carries weaker source evidence than an annotated tag. Cost to operate, throughput and observed visibility within the declared deadline are all that is claimed: no durability, no accept==stored and no equivalence. Storage is the unmatched profile and resources the enforced 2 CPU / 2 GiB cgroup v2 profile, in which the CPU budget is a ceiling and not a reservation and memory.current includes reclaimable cache beside anon; both are stated in every report. Targets without a verified server search are scanned completely and filtered on the client, and GreenMail is read over POP3 in this draft; both are labelled per row.
